title: Prefill-first Kernel Search with Multi-fidelity Cost Model and Decode Pipelining
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a practical, low-risk kernel-selection and scheduling pipeline that preferentially optimizes prefill execution while respecting decode tail-latency SLOs across heterogeneous GPU fleets. Motivation: many workloads are prefill-heavy (long prompts) and existing autotuners focus on decode or single-fidelity profiling. Approach: 1) Train a multi-fidelity neural cost model that combines very cheap microbenchmarks (per-arch / small input kernels), sparse high-fidelity traces (end-to-end prefill+decode), and histogram summaries of incoming sequence-length distributions per route. 2) Use a population-based simulated-annealing search over kernel portfolios constrained by memory/occupancy and per-device kernel availability. 3) Integrate a prefill-first scheduler that reserves KV cache warm-pools, issues speculative kernel warmups, and overlaps prefill microbatches with decode work by device affinity. 4) Add safety constraints (fallback to verified kernel for tail events) and continuous regret monitoring to retract suboptimal selections. Success metrics: 95th percentile latency improvement for prefill-heavy routes >= 10% and unit token cost improvement >= 6% without increasing decode 99th percentile beyond 5% of baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Multi-fidelity cost model trained and evaluated: RMSE < 10% on held-out high-fidelity traces
Automated search produces stable kernel portfolios for at least three representative routes and decreases measured prefill P95 by >= 10% in lab A/B
Canary rollout completed on runtime-1.21 with automatic rollback if decode P99 regression > 5% or error rate increases
experiments: E1: Collect baseline microbenchmarks (per-arch/op/k seqlen grid) and 72h production trace sample for two routes
E2: Train cost model (tiny MLP + ordinal embedding for seqlen buckets) using multi-fidelity loss (cheap microbench + weighted high-fidelity traces)
E3: Implement population-based simulated annealing search with occupancy constraints and sample the top-5 portfolios per device class
E4: Implement prefill-first scheduler that pre-allocates KV pools and issues speculative kernel warmups; measure overlap efficiency
E5: Run lab A/B for three routes (chat, search-rerank, long-form generation) across A100/H100-equivalent fleets
E6: Canary deployment to 3% traffic with telemetry (latency histograms, cost per token, kernel switch counts)
